required_columns.description: Globally unique mesh-manifest row identifier.
Study-scoped human donor identifier.
Stable DOI, PMID, repository accession, or primary-study identifier.
Exact specimen, image volume, segmentation, and repository locator.
Calibration, internal validation, or independent held-out assignment.
Must be Homo sapiens.
Must explicitly establish healthy/non-diseased liver context.
Measured zonation assignment or explicit unresolved token.
In-situ tissue, precision-cut slice, isolated PHH, or other exact preparation.
Fixation, clearing, embedding, sectioning, and shrinkage-correction context.
Exact microscopy/tomography modality.
Raw x voxel spacing in micrometres.
Raw y voxel spacing in micrometres.
Raw z voxel spacing in micrometres.
Segmentation algorithm, version, model, and manual-correction protocol.
One exact target_structure_id.
Physical cell or organelle instance identifier.
Biological replicate identity; not a synthetic donor.
Repository-relative canonical triangle-mesh JSON path.
SHA-256 of the exact canonical mesh artifact.
Must be um; no implicit scale conversion is allowed.
Exact specimen/cell-fixed coordinate frame.
Frozen transform into the declared cell reference frame.
Measured target used to register the mesh.
Raw topology QC status from the supplying pipeline.
Pass/fail status from a named geometric self-intersection audit.
Exact external audit tool and version.
Frozen external geometric self-intersection report.
Checksum of the frozen self-intersection report.
Segmentation, registration, voxel and boundary uncertainty.
Must be pass before scientific promotion.

conditional_columns.description: Containing cell or parent organelle instance.
Checksum required with a domain annotation artifact.
Measured cell-cell or cell-pathogen interface surface.
Checksum required with contact-interface ground truth.
Identifier for mechanics measured in the same donor/cell context.
Frozen grid-convergence report for this registered mesh.
Checksum required with a grid-convergence report.
Truncation, field-of-view, occlusion, or missing-structure status.
